body.en: Linear equations, systems, and inequalities form the largest tested domain on the EST I. Fluency here is non-negotiable for a high score.

Slope-intercept form: \( y = mx + b \). Slope: \( m = \dfrac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1} \). Solve systems by substitution or elimination. For inequalities, flip the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative.

Solve the system: \( 2x+y=7 \), \( x-y=2 \).

Adding: \( 3x=9 \), so \( x=3 \), \( y=1 \).

Linear inequalities

A linear inequality such as \( 2x-3 > 7 \) is solved like an equation, but the solution is a range: \( x > 5 \). On a number line, use an open circle for strict inequalities (\( > \), \( < \)) and a closed circle for \( \geq \) or \( \leq \).

caption.en: Graphical representation of the linear system \(y = 2x - 1\) and \(y = -x + 5\). The unique solution is the point of intersection \((2, 3)\).

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Linear Equations & Systems

body.en:
• Inequality Sign Flip: When multiplying or dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number, you MUST reverse the inequality symbol: \(-3x < 12 \implies x > -4\).
  • Infinite vs. No Solution: If solving leads to a true statement like \(0 = 0\), the system has infinitely many solutions (coincident lines). If it leads to a contradiction like \(0 = 7\), there is no solution (parallel lines).
  • Slope from Standard Form: For \(Ax + By = C\), the slope is \(m = -A/B\) and the \(y\)-intercept is \(C/B\). Do not forget the negative sign on \(A/B\)!
  • Absolute Value Splitting: The equation \(|2x - 5| = 9\) splits into two distinct equations: \(2x - 5 = 9\) OR \(2x - 5 = -9\). If an absolute value equals a negative number (e.g. \(|x + 3| = -4\)), there is immediately NO solution.

solution.en: From second equation: \(x = y+2\). Substitute: \(3(y+2)+2y=16 \Rightarrow 5y=10 \Rightarrow y=2, x=4\).

question.en: A school theater sold 250 tickets for a play, raising a total of $1,750. Adult tickets cost $9 each and student tickets cost $5 each. How many adult tickets were sold?

solution.en:
Set up system of equations: Let \(a\) be the number of adult tickets and \(s\) be student tickets: \[ \begin{cases} a + s = 250 \\ 9a + 5s = 1750 \end{cases} \]

Elimination method: Multiply the first equation by 5: \[ 5a + 5s = 1250. \] Subtract from the second equation: \[ (9a + 5s) - (5a + 5s) = 1750 - 1250 \implies 4a = 500 \implies a = 125. \]

Exactly 125 adult tickets were sold (and \(s = 250 - 125 = 125\) student tickets).
